cohort: The study included 61 women who underwent laparoscopic excision of ureteral endometriosis, excluding those who had hysterectomy/bilateral adnexectomy, were lost to follow-up, or had less than 1 year of follow-up.
finding: Fertility rates after laparoscopic ureterolysis are comparable to other forms of deep endometriosis, and despite a higher risk of caesarean and preterm birth, the overall course of pregnancy and peripartum outcomes appear encouraging.
mod_finding: The study found a higher risk of caesarean sections (40.9%) among women who became pregnant after laparoscopic ureterolysis.
gest_age: Median gestational week at delivery was 38 weeks + 2 days (range, 33 + 1-41 + 6).
